title: The Lobster Nebula seen with ESO’s VISTA telescope
caption: The Lobster Nebula, NGC 6357, imaged by ESO's VISTA survey telescope
celestial: NGC 6357 · constellation Scorpius · about 8000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESO/VVV Survey/D. Minniti. Acknowledgement: Ignacio Toledo

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Huge clouds of glowing gas, laced with threads of dust, surround hot young stars in this infrared landscape from ESO's VISTA telescope. The scene is NGC 6357, a stellar nursery known as the Lobster Nebula.

Infrared light changes the view because it passes through dust much more easily than visible light. Stars that are hidden or dimmed in ordinary photographs can shine through, and the structure of the clouds around them looks different. For a stellar nursery, where young stars are often still wrapped in the material that formed them, that is a big advantage.

The image comes from a survey called VVV, short for VISTA Variables in the Vía Láctea. That survey is scanning the Milky Way in an effort to map our galaxy's structure and explain how it formed, so this picture is a by-product of a much larger project. It was recorded through J, H and Ks filters in the near-infrared. The official caption offers few further details about the nebula itself.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (90.92 x 90.92 arcminutes) and distance (8000 light years), the frame spans roughly 212 × 212 light-years. Its light set out about 8,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a near-infrared image from VISTA's VIRCAM camera, taken through J, H and Ks filters. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
